record.original_question: Further develop the theory of program-size complexity for infinite computations, and in particular clarify its relation to algorithmic probability.

evidence.quote: 8. Further develop the theory of program-size complexity for infinite computations. Particularly, study the relations between program-size complexity and algorithmic probability. (G. J. Chaitin)

artifact.status_search_result: Program-size complexity for infinite computations has been studied (e.g., via Turing machines with infinite output, monotone complexity KM, a priori complexity KA, and process complexity), but a complete theory unifying these with algorithmic probability for non-halting computations remains active research. No single definitive resolution of Chaitin's program is reported; the question is generally treated as an ongoing research direction.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses monotone and a priori complexities for infinite sequences, noting these are distinct notions whose relations are still being investigated.
status_evidence.claim: Multiple complexity notions for infinite sequences exist and their relations to algorithmic probability remain a research topic.

status_evidence.snippet: Chaitin's Omega encodes halting probability; relations between program-size complexity for infinite outputs and algorithmic probability continue to be studied.
status_evidence.claim: The theory of program-size complexity for infinite computations remains an active area connected to Chaitin's program.

Let $U$ be a fixed universal prefix-free Turing machine. For a finite binary string $x$, the prefix-free program-size complexity is
$$H(x) = \min\{|p| : U(p) = x\},$$
and the algorithmic probability of $x$ is
$$P(x) = \sum_{p:\, U(p)=x} 2^{-|p|}.$$
A classical theorem of Levin–Chaitin asserts that $H(x) = -\log_2 P(x) + O(1)$.

Consider now Turing machines that perform infinite computations, i.e. computations that never halt but produce (or attempt to produce) an infinite binary sequence on a one-way output tape. For such machines several natural notions of program-size complexity can be defined for an infinite sequence $\omega \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$, for instance:
\begin{itemize}
\item $H^{\infty}(\omega) = \min\{|p| : U^{\infty}(p) \text{ writes out } \omega\}$, where $U^{\infty}$ is a fixed universal machine performing infinite computations;
\item $H^{\infty}_{\le n}(\omega)$, the minimal program length needed for $U^{\infty}$ to output an initial segment of $\omega$ of length at least $n$;
\item the corresponding algorithmic probability $P^{\infty}(\omega) = \sum_{p:\, U^{\infty}(p) \text{ outputs } \omega} 2^{-|p|}$, suitably interpreted as a measure on Cantor space.
\end{itemize}

Problem. Develop the theory of program-size complexity for infinite computations. In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Give a robust, machine-independent definition of program-size complexity $H^{\infty}$ for infinite binary sequences produced by non-halting computations, and identify the invariance properties analogous to those of the classical $H$.
\item Define an appropriate notion of algorithmic probability $P^{\infty}$ for infinite sequences in this setting.
\item Establish the precise quantitative relation between $H^{\infty}$ and $P^{\infty}$, and determine to what extent the Levin–Chaitin coincidence $H = -\log_2 P + O(1)$ extends, fails, or must be modified for infinite computations.
